why: A has accurate page citations and more substantive critical points: SOAP is never tested at 72B or 100M, Algorithm 1 omits the 0.2 factor, and the FP32/BF16 conflict. It wrongly says appendices are missing. B has two bad page cites and fewer insights.

wrong.claim: Appendix A.3, which supports Eq. 4's conditioning claim, is 'not in this text'
wrong.pdf: Appendix A.3 is printed in the PDF and derives κ(S_KL) = √κ(S_Shampoo) (Eq. 13)

wrong.claim: MXFP8 results are in Appendix B, 'which is not in this text'
wrong.pdf: Appendix B and Table 7 (BF16 vs MXFP8, plus Lion) are printed in the PDF

only_here: Algorithm 1 scales only by √max(in,out) and omits the ≈0.2 RMS factor stated in the text
Optimizer step is said to be 'always FP32', yet Newton–Schulz is said to run in BF16
The 621M model used in the instability study is not among the models listed in Sec. 5.1
SOAP is never run on the 72B model or at 100M-token batches, so the abstract's SOAP claims overreach
Table 3 does not say whether its max LRs belong to AdamW or to each optimizer
Ramp-up parameters S and N are never given numerically
The layer-wise optimizer lacks TP support for SOAP (stated limitation)
Training loss is claimed to correlate with validation loss, but validation loss is never shown
Full Nano-V3 Math Avg numbers and the 72B Commonsense Avg comparison
Muon 3× is below Muon 2× on Nano-V3 Math Avg as well
AdamW 1× also wins GSM8k CoT on the 72B model and MBPP+ on Nano-V3
Inconsistency: p.13 says the current-gradient fix 'was present with SOAP', while p.11 says the reference SOAP omits it
Confound: Figs. 1–2 compare large-batch Muon with ramp-up against 1× AdamW
On the 621M model the oscillations eventually damp out
No seeds or error bars; no wall-clock or memory cost reported for per-step QR
Descriptions of how the duplicated and distributed TP modes work
